description:
Round-29 perf lever (docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Â§A.4).

=== DONE (s470bu) ===

THE MEASUREMENT that found it.  `sb-sprof` over the `regexg` bench row
(`while ($x =~ /./g)` over 200 000 chars), 16 179 samples, my own tree:

  sxhash-recurse (in perhaps-truncated-equal-hash)  6.8 % self
  sb-impl::gethash/equal                            4.8 % self, 16.8 % total
  %sxhash-string/truncating                         2.5 %
  equal-not-inline                                  1.6 %
  pcl::%p-regex-op                                  3.0 %

`(p-regex :pat "." :flags "g" :tier :native)` expanded to `(%p-regex-op "."
"g")`, and `%p-regex-op` memoizes on `(list flags raw)` â so a match in a loop
CONSED a fresh two-element list and did an EQUAL gethash on it (sxhash of a
list of two strings, then an `equal` compare) on EVERY evaluation, to look up
a struct that a compile-time-constant pattern can only ever have one of.
`%p-subst-parts` and `%p-tr-parts` were worse in a different way: they have no
memo at all and ALLOCATE A FRESH OP STRUCT per evaluation (`%p-flag-keywords`
interning one keyword per modifier letter each time).

THE FIX, on #1180 `symref-const`'s precedent: one per-call-site cell.

  %p-literal-op-text FORM  -- the STRING a regex-literal keyword denotes AT
    MACROEXPANSION TIME, or NIL.  Exactly two shapes carry one: a string
    literal, and `(p-esc "â¦")` (the IR's escaped-payload wrapper, which p-esc
    itself decodes at macroexpansion â so this is the same reading, not a
    second one).  `(p-string-concat â¦)`, a variable, a hash element: NIL.

  %p-op-once FORM  -- FORM evaluated at most once for the site it expands at,
    remembered in `(load-time-value (cons nil nil) nil)`.

`p-regex`, `p-subst` and `p-tr` wrap their constructor in `%p-op-once` when
EVERY ingredient is a compile-time string.  `p-qr` deliberately does NOT: two
evaluations of `qr/a/` are distinct references in perl (ir-spec Â§10), which is
why `%p-qr-parts` was never memoized either.

WHY LAZY AND NOT `(load-time-value (%p-regex-op â¦) t)`.  The constructor can
ANNOUNCE â `%pcl-strip-regex-code-blocks` writes to stderr when it strips a
`(?{code})` block â and `parse-regex-modifiers` can reject a letter.  A
load-time-value would move both to the LOAD of the file, so a site that never
executes would announce (or die).  The site cell keeps them at the first
EXECUTION, exactly where they are today.

WHY CACHING THE OP IS NOT OBSERVABLE.
  m//   `%p-regex-op` already returns a GLOBALLY memoized struct, so the site
        cell answers the very same object it answered before.  Zero change.
  s///  the op was fresh per evaluation, but `do-regex-subst` only READS it
        (an s/// op is not a value a perl program can hold â `p-=~` consumes
        it), so one shared struct per site is the same computation.  A
        replacement that is a CLOSURE keeps the fresh op: it may capture
        lexicals, and `%p-op-once` would freeze the first capture.
  tr/// `do-tr` likewise only reads its op.

MEASURED (`scratch/s470bu/ab-rt.pl` â ONE transpiled program against TWO
runtimes, two cores, interleaved, best-of-5, startup subtracted):

  regexg    base 0.9511 s -> 0.7473 s   **-21.4 %**
  textproc  base 2.5385 s -> 2.3110 s   **-9.0 %**  (a MACRO row)
  control (two byte-identical runtimes, same window):  -1.0 %

and the hand-replaced ceiling taken BEFORE writing any code (`ab-lisp.pl`,
the same program with the op hoisted out of the loop by hand): **-20.8 %**,
byte-identical control pair +0.1 %.  So the lever collects essentially all of
its ceiling.

BARS.  Guard `Pl/t/perf-levers-03.t` rows 1/2/5/8 with FIVE negatives beside
them (an interpolated m// pattern, `p-regex-from-parts`, a closure
replacement, an interpolated s/// pattern, `p-qr`); inverse-verified on a
`git archive e25c2280` extraction, where exactly those four rows fail.  15
regex/subst/tr shapes probed against perl 5.40.3, identical.  RUNTIME-ONLY:
`pl2cl`'s output does not change, so corpus-diff is IDENTICAL and there is no
`PCL_OPT` name and no generation bump (the #1181 / #1203-#1205 precedent).


BARS TAKEN JOINTLY WITH #1251 (s470bu, resumed run, 2026-09-06).
One gate covers both levers, which are the only two commits on the branch:
gate `PCLXS_DIR=~/pclxs tools/prove-core` 216 files / 7478 rows, FAIL = exactly
the 13 standing pclxs xs rows; full sweep `--jobs 4` GATE clean (0 new / 0 fixed /
0 LOST after the serial re-run, TOTAL passing 18649 = baseline +0, drops 5 =
census, shortfall +0); ir-conform 289 pass / 0 fail / 56 known / 0 stale;
corpus-diff vs 31473881 IDENTICAL over 111 files (silent drops 5, unchanged);
emission-ab --shapes --list lib/**/*.pm 27/27 SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF;
tag-license --check clean; ir-host-leak unchanged (same corpus emission).
Companion `--jobs 1` over re/regexp.t re/subst.t re/substT.t re/subst_amp.t
re/pat.t op/tr.t op/split.t op/quotemeta.t, BEFORE = a `git archive 31473881`
extraction: every row identical; the single status flip (re/regexp.t
TIMEOUT -> DIFF at the SAME 797/108 counts) did not reproduce on a serial
re-run of either tree, so it was load noise and nothing was spliced.
Guards re-verified after the rebase onto 31473881: `Pl/t/perf-levers-03.t`
18/18 green here, and on the extraction rows 1/2/5/7/10/12/13/14/15 FAIL
while the six negatives and the three RUN rows pass.

The macro numbers were re-taken on a QUIET box (load 1.99) against main
31473881's runtime: regexg 1.5295 -> 1.1602 s (-24.1 %), textproc
3.7141 -> 2.8516 (-23.2 %); controls intloop+= -1.9 %, strcat -1.0 %,
sortstr +1.2 %, moo-objs +0.5 %.
